amendments.rule: **A verb the ASV renders as a light verb plus a complement heads on the complement, not on the light verb.** This is rule 31's test applied to a verb: drop each word in turn, and the head is the one whose loss loses the lexeme. `הַאֲזִין` → *Give ear unto* heads on *ear*, because *give* alone gives anything; so too `הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה` → *did obeisance*, `נוֹעַץ` → *took counsel*, `הִמְלִיךְ` → *make king*, `הוֹדָה` → *give thanks*, `כִּלָּה` → *made an end*, `עוּד` → *bear witness*, `חָנַן` → *make supplication*, `בּוֹשׁ` → *put to shame*. The complement need not be a noun: an adjective (`הִכְבִּיד` → *made heavy*, `גָּדַל` → *make greater*) and a second verb (`חָטָא` hiphil → *made to sin*, `אָכַל` → *did eat*) are read the same way. Rule 24's *lexical predicate over subjects and auxiliaries* is about `was gathered`, and must not be read as a preference for the English verb — that reasoning would head *make king* on *make*. **A phrasal particle is not a complement.** `שָׁלַח` → *put forth*, `סוּר` → *take away*, and `נָתַן` → *put away* are one lexical verb plus its particle, and the head stays on the verb; the same subtraction says so, since *forth* and *away* alone name nothing. **A supplied object is not a complement either.** Where the ASV writes an object pronoun inside such a rendering — `וַיַּפֵּל` → *he let* ***it*** *fall*, `וַיַּשְׁקְ` → *gave* ***them*** *drink* — read whether an object morpheme is present. Where one is, it takes the pronoun under rule 18 and the verb keeps the rest, as in `וַיַּעֲבִירֵם` → *caused* ***them*** *to pass through*. Where none is, the pronoun answers to no morpheme, is its own `added` unit under rule 30, and does not join the verb merely because it stands inside its rendering; the verb's unit is discontinuous around it under rule 25. **This applies only to a pronoun that truly supplies an object.** A reflexive pronoun the ASV uses to render the Hebrew verb's own voice is part of that verb's unit, because the source verb licenses it: `אִכַּף` → *bow myself* keeps *myself* with the Niphal verb and heads on *bow*. Position inside the English verb phrase is not what makes a word part of the verb's rendering — the complement or the source verb's voice must license it, and an unsupported object does not. **But a preposition the ASV supplies to reach the verb's own object is part of that rendering.** Where the Hebrew writes a bare direct object — no object marker on it and no preposition of its own — and the English verb reaches that object through a preposition the ASV has written, the preposition belongs to the verb's unit and not to the object noun's: `חָמְסוּ תוֹרָתִי` → *have done violence* ***to*** *my law*, `תְּבַצְּעִי רֵעַיִךְ` → *hast greedily gained* ***of*** *thy neighbors*, `הֵקַלּוּ אָב וָאֵם` → *have set light* ***by*** *father and mother*, `אֲבַקֵּשׁ אִישׁ` → *sought* ***for*** *a man*, `טָחוּ תָּפֵל` → *have daubed ... with untempered mortar*. This is rule 16's reasoning where no marker stands to take the word: the same subtraction test finds that dropping it diminishes nothing but the object relation, and the object noun's own English is the noun. The unit is discontinuous under rule 25 where other material stands between the verb and the preposition, and the head is unaffected — it stays on the lexical verb, or on the complement where this rule's light-verb clause puts it. Two limits. Where an object marker or a preposition of the object's own is present, that morpheme takes the word under rules 16 and 11, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied reading does. And this does not touch rule 33: a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative is licensed by that noun's own case-function and stays with the noun, whereas a word supplied for a direct object is licensed by the English verb's valency, so read which the Hebrew noun is before placing it.
amendments.why: EZK.22 met this construction five times — 22.7, 22.12, 22.26, 22.28, 22.30 — and analysed 22.28 the other way from the rest, which is the split this pass patched. The contract gives no rule for it: rule 16 states the principle (such a preposition 'is the marker's rendering, not the object noun's ... it exists only to attach the object to the verb') but only for H853, and says nothing about a clause where no marker stands. Rule 33 pulls the opposite way for adverbial accusatives, so the two are distinguished explicitly rather than left to a later reader. It is put on rule 44 rather than raised as a new rule because rule 44 is already where the contract decides what does and does not belong inside a verb's rendering — phrasal particles in, supplied objects out, reflexives in — and a qualification hung off rule 16 would leave that rule's marker-only scope reading as though it settled the no-marker case. Nothing in the corpus tables supplied contradicts it; they are keyed by source lemma, so a preposition with no source token of its own appears in none of them.

conventions: Where the Hebrew writes a bare direct object, with no object marker and no preposition on it, and the ASV supplies an English preposition for the verb to reach that object, the preposition joins the verb's unit rather than the object noun's: הֵקַלּוּ -> *set light by* (22.7), תְּבַצְּעִי -> *greedily gained of* (22.12), חָמְסוּ -> *have done violence to* (22.26), טָחוּ -> *daubed ... with* (22.28), אֲבַקֵּשׁ -> *sought for* (22.30). This is rule 16's reasoning applied where no marker stands to take the word, and the head is unaffected. It does not touch rule 33: a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative stays with the noun whose case-function licenses it.

The lexicalized 1cs suffix of אֲדֹנָי receives no separate English pronoun and is its own unrepresented unit throughout the chapter (22.3, 22.12, 22.19, 22.28, 22.31), the construct noun taking the supplied *the* under rule 29. BSB represents this suffix and so disagrees at all five, which is a convention difference and not an error.

לָכֵן (22.19 twice) and עַל־כֵּן (22.4) are fused units under rule 30, each headed on the preposition as the morpheme carrying the causal relation. Heading them on כֵּן is defensible and is named in the unit notes; the chapter takes the preposition uniformly, and a later reader should not split the difference between the three occurrences.

report: One real cross-verse split: the English preposition the ASV supplies to reach a bare Hebrew direct object, where no object marker and no Hebrew preposition stands on that object. EZK.22.7 (set light by), 22.12 (greedily gained of), 22.26 (have done violence to) and 22.30 (sought for) all keep that preposition inside the verb's unit, on rule 16's reasoning that it realizes the object relation rather than the noun. EZK.22.28 alone put the *with* of טָחוּ ... תָּפֵל -> *have daubed for them with untempered mortar* into the object noun's unit. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: תָּפֵל is as bare an accusative as תּוֹרָתִי. 22.28 is patched to match the other four; only t008 moves, and תָּפֵל keeps *untempered mortar*, still headed on *untempered* under rule 31.

Everything else in the candidate table is context rather than a split. לְמַעַן -> *to* (22.6, 9, 12) against *that* (22.27) is rule 52 reading an infinitival rendering against a finite one. בְּ + suffix unrepresented at 22.5 (shall mock thee) against *in thee* in eight verses is rule 40's promotion of the object. אֵת -> *with* at 22.14 (deal with thee) against unrepresented at 22.15 (scatter thee) is rule 16's first family against rule 16's default. הָיָה -> have been / is become / are become / they are tracks plain predication, the resultative הָיָה לְ (22.18, 22.19, with לְ unrepresented in both under rule 21), and a gapped copula. The waws rendered *Moreover* (22.1) against *And* (22.17, 22.23) in the identical word-formula are rule 14 read off the ASV.

Supplied English was checked verse against verse in the dump, since the lemma table is blind to added units. It agrees throughout: a supplied *the* and a supplied relative fold into the noun or attributive they serve (22.18, 22.24, 22.25, 22.27, 22.30, and the three articleless attributives at 22.3, 22.24, 22.30); a supplied object pronoun with no object morpheme is added (22.3 her, 22.14 it twice, 22.20 it); a supplied lexical causee is added (22.26 men); a supplied possessive with no suffix is added (22.10 their); an ASV-italic *and* with no waw is added (22.5, 22.27). Article counting is consistent too: two ASV *the*s give one to the article and one to the construct (22.29 the people of the land), one gives it to the article alone (22.2 the bloody city), and none leaves the article unrepresented (22.5, 22.7, 22.12).

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences and none is a genuine error. The R cluster is לֵאמֹר's לְ under rule 27 plus prepositions the ASV's recasting silences under rules 21 and 40; the Sp1cs cluster is the lexicalized suffix of אֲדֹנָי; the To cluster is rule 16's default with the object written bare; EZK.22.5's article and the two EZK.22.24 pronouns are places the ASV writes nothing at all. No accepted edge was changed to move the rate.

Three conventions recorded, and one amendment offered to rule 44 covering the construction the patch settles. The chapter's other named ties (לָכֵן headed on the preposition, *every one* headed on *one*, the three distributed *you*s of 22.20, *there* kept inside the verb at 22.20) are internally consistent and were left as accepted.
